description: Tamagoyaki is a beloved Japanese rolled omelette, known for its distinct sweet and savory flavor and beautiful layered texture. This staple of Japanese breakfast and bento boxes offers a delightful culinary experience, showcasing the chef's delicate touch. Master this iconic dish to bring an authentic taste of Japan to your table.

instructions.title: Prepare the Egg Mixture
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, gently whisk the eggs until just combined, being careful not to incorporate too much air. In a separate small bowl, combine the dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt. Stir until the sugar and salt are fully dissolved. Add this seasoned dashi mixture to the whisked eggs and mix gently. Strain the egg mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any chalazae or foam, ensuring a smooth omelette.

instructions.title: Heat the Tamagoyaki Pan
instructions.text: Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or a small non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat. Lightly coat the pan with a thin layer of vegetable oil using a paper towel dipped in oil. Ensure the entire surface is evenly greased.

instructions.title: Pour the First Layer
instructions.text: Pour about one-quarter of the egg mixture into the hot pan, tilting the pan to spread the egg evenly into a thin layer. Cook for about 1-2 minutes until the edges are set and the top is mostly set but still slightly wet.

instructions.title: Roll the First Layer
instructions.text: Using chopsticks or a spatula, gently roll the cooked egg layer from one end of the pan to the other. Push the rolled egg to one side of the pan, leaving space for the next layer.

instructions.title: Add Subsequent Layers
instructions.text: Re-oil the empty section of the pan if necessary. Pour another one-quarter of the egg mixture into the pan, lifting the previously rolled egg slightly to allow the new mixture to flow underneath it. Cook until mostly set, then roll the cooked portion towards the already rolled egg, incorporating the new layer. Repeat this process with the remaining egg mixture, adding new layers and rolling until all the egg is used and forms a thick, multi-layered omelette.

instructions.title: Shape and Rest the Omelette
instructions.text: Once all the egg mixture is rolled, gently press the tamagoyaki against the sides of the pan with your spatula to square off its shape. Remove the finished tamagoyaki from the pan and place it on a bamboo rolling mat (makisu) or a cutting board. Wrap it tightly in the mat or simply let it rest for a few minutes. This helps it retain its shape and firm up.

instructions.title: Slice and Serve
instructions.text: Once slightly cooled and firm, slice the tamagoyaki into 1-inch thick pieces. Arrange on a plate and serve warm or at room temperature. It makes an excellent addition to a Japanese breakfast, bento box, or as a snack.

tips: For the best texture, use a rectangular tamagoyaki pan. If you dont have one, a small non-stick round pan will work, but the shape will be different.
Strain the egg mixture to remove any air bubbles or bits of chalazae; this results in a smoother, more uniform omelette.
Control the heat carefully. If the pan is too hot, the egg will cook too quickly and brown. If it's too cool, it will take too long to set and may tear.
